issues.legal_issue: An application to reject a plaint must be decided from the plaint’s averments, without relying on pleas or materials supplied by the defendant.
material_facts: The defendant applied to reject the plaint, relying in part on grounds drawn from the defence and materials outside the plaint.
The trial court allowed the application, but the appellate court set that order aside and remitted the case for consideration of all issues.
issues.conclusion: The plaint’s averments alone could be examined on the application; the defendant’s written-statement pleas were irrelevant. The High Court was justified in affirming the remittal for consideration of all issues.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the court examines the averments in the plaint and does not rely on the defendant’s written statement. The Court relied on C. Natrajan v. Ashim Bai, (2007) 14 SCC 183; Ram Prakash Gupta v. Rajiv Kumar Gupta, (2007) 10 SCC 59; Hardesh Ores (P) Ltd. v. Hede and Company, (2007) 5 SCC 614; Mayar (H.K.) Ltd. v. Owners & Parties, Vessel M.V. Fortune Express, (2006) 3 SCC 100; Sopan Sukhdeo Sable v. Assistant Charity Commissioner, (2004) 3 SCC 137; Saleem Bhai v. State of Maharashtra, (2003) 1 SCC 557; and The Church of Christ Charitable Trust & Educational Charitable Society v. M/s Ponniamman Educational Trust, 2012 (6) JT 149.

predicates.plaint_rejection_application: A defendant applied for rejection of a plaint.
predicates.defendant_submitted_defence_material: The defendant submitted or relied on material from the defence rather than relying only on the plaint.

issues.definition: When a defendant applies to reject a plaint and relies on defence material, the application is decided from the plaint’s allegations alone.

issues.legal_issue: A previous proceeding dismissed for default or withdrawn does not bar a current suit where the earlier proceeding has been restored and the suits concern different properties.
material_facts: A previous suit was dismissed for default and later restored, and it remained pending when the defendant applied to reject the current plaint.
The relief in the previous suit and the relief in the current suit concerned different properties.
The defendant relied on the earlier proceedings to argue that the current plaint was barred.
issues.conclusion: The provisions concerning dismissal for default and withdrawal did not bar the current suit on these facts. The case was properly remitted for the trial court to consider all issues.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that Order IX Rules 8 and 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 did not apply because the earlier suit had been restored and was pending; in any event, the earlier and current suits concerned different properties. For the same reasons, Order XXIII Rule 1(3) and Rule 4(b) did not apply.

predicates.plaint_rejection_application: A defendant applied for rejection of a plaint.
predicates.earlier_suit_dismissed_for_default_and_r: An earlier suit was dismissed for default and later restored.
predicates.different_properties: The earlier suit and the current suit concerned different properties.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks rejection of a plaint based on an earlier suit that was dismissed for default and restored, and the suits concern different properties, the earlier proceeding does not bar the current suit.
